purpose: Response-free known-truth experiment to causally test two proposed moderators of structural predictive added value: reference saturation and response-aligned refreshing.

levels.weak: baseline contains only local x/y and context sin/cos
levels.strong: baseline additionally contains the exact current structural latent state used by the generating process

reference_saturation.causal_question: Does structural augmentation lose incremental value when the reference already contains the relevant structural information?

levels.refreshed: Layer-B representation uses the current context-specific structural latent state
levels.static_reused: Layer-B representation for each node is averaged over fitting contexts and reused across all contexts

response_alignment.causal_question: Does a static representation lose value when structural truth changes across response contexts?

design.split: first 60 nodes x first 12 contexts fit; last 20 nodes x last 8 contexts score

known_truth.refreshed_layer_b: eight fixed nonlinear transforms of current structural_latent_state, x, y and context phase
known_truth.static_reuse_intervention: for each node, average its refreshed Layer-B vector across the 12 fitting contexts and reuse this vector in every context
known_truth.strong_reference_intervention: append the exact current structural_latent_state to the conventional baseline; this deliberately saturates the reference with the generating structural signal

cell_estimand: augmented minus matched baseline log loss within the same reference-saturation level and replicate; negative values favor structural augmentation

primary_estimands.weak_refreshed_added_value: added value under weak baseline and refreshed Layer B
primary_estimands.saturation_moderation: added_value(strong,refreshed) - added_value(weak,refreshed); positive means benefit shrinks when reference is saturated
primary_estimands.alignment_moderation: added_value(weak,static_reused) - added_value(weak,refreshed); positive means benefit shrinks under static reuse

interpretation_if_any_check_fail: known_truth_partial_support_or_refutation; do not retune the generator or thresholds to force the two-moderator story
forbidden_interpretations: Synthetic effect magnitudes estimate A-Islands, Tanzania, Azores, Louisiana or Tampa effect sizes
Passing proves the moderators explain the historical cross-system signs
Passing authorizes rescue or rerun of any consumed empirical endpoint
Passing changes the closed EOG-WF denominator
Failing authorizes changing the frozen generating truth or success thresholds
